The xlayer-reth Cargo.lock at tag v0.0.7.3 pins okx/reth rev 81573d2c (lines 8171, 8212, 8239) and the lock at v0.0.7.3-rc.1 pins f60420aa at the same lines. web3_clientVersion on https://rpc.xlayer.tech returned reth/v2.3.0-f60420a/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/xlayer/v0.0.7 on 2026-11-25. The release dates and the mandatory-patch wording on the GitHub releases page could not be read in this session because github.com HTML is blocked by the proxy; that link stays unconfirmed by me. verdicts.codeCheck: The change is in the node's state root walk. The cited src/PoolManager.sol:104-114 is unlock and is not affected by a trie walk: the EVM results, storage writes and settlement do not depend on how the node hashes the trie. A node on the final tag would compute a different state root for an affected layout and stop following, so readers of that node see stale state. No PoolManager line computes a different value.
verdicts.corrections: severity: low. The finding describes an operational hazard (a follower node that may stall or fork and serve stale pool state) with no loss path, which SCHEMA.md places at low rather than info. Actor operator is correct.

clearedSpotChecks.check: ruint 1.18.0 (X Layer) shift and SAR code against RUSTSEC-2026-0220
clearedSpotChecks.note: The advisory text says the affected wrapping_shl and wrapping_shr truncate shift amounts modulo 2^32 and that the wrong overflow flags concern checked and saturating variants. revm-interpreter 37.0.3 src/instructions/bitwise.rs lines 120-158 (read from the crate) saturates the shift to usize and only calls the library when shift < 256, returning zero or the sign fill otherwise. On chain I ran SHL, SHR and SAR for 6 words and 19 shift amounts including 2^32, 2^32+1, 2^32+255, 2^64, 2^128 and 2^256-1 through eth_call on forno.celo.org and rpc.xlayer.tech: 342 checks per chain, 0 mismatches.

clearedSpotChecks.note: The same on-chain shift vectors on forno.celo.org matched the EVM definition with 0 mismatches, including amounts at 63, 64, 127, 128, 129, 191, 192 and 255 where the u128 half split acts.
